## Company Research: Anthropic

### One-liner
Anthropic is an AI safety company building reliable, interpretable AI systems, best known for creating Claude.

### What they do
Anthropic develops frontier AI models with a focus on safety research. Their flagship product Claude powers consumer apps and API services used by thousands of businesses. They are a well-funded AI lab competing with OpenAI and Google DeepMind.

### Recent news
- [2026-03] Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 4.6 with 1M context window (Source: anthropic.com)
- [2025-11] Series E funding at $18B valuation (Source: techcrunch.com)
- [2026-01] Launched Claude for Enterprise with enhanced security controls (Source: anthropic.com)

### Culture & values
Anthropic emphasizes safety-first AI development, academic rigor, and a mission-driven culture. Engineers work closely with safety researchers. Remote-friendly with offices in San Francisco and London.

### Sources
- https://anthropic.com/about
- https://techcrunch.com/anthropic
- https://anthropic.com/claude

payload.title: Cover Letter
payload.content_markdown:
Dear Anthropic Hiring Team,

Anthropic's recent launch of Claude for Enterprise — and the engineering challenge of serving safety-aligned AI at massive scale — is exactly the infrastructure problem I've spent four years building toward.

At Acme Corp, I built and owned FastAPI services handling 2M daily requests, backed by PostgreSQL and Redis, deployed on AWS via Kubernetes. I cut deploy times by 60% with GitHub Actions pipelines and most recently built a LangChain-based RAG system for internal knowledge retrieval — directly adjacent to the AI infrastructure work your team is doing. My experience productionizing PyTorch models at StartupXYZ adds the ML-side context needed to be a genuine partner to your safety researchers, not just an API plumber.

What draws me specifically to Anthropic is the mission discipline. You're the team that published the Constitutional AI paper and treats safety as an engineering constraint, not an afterthought. That combination of frontier capability with rigorous safety thinking is rare, and it's where I want to spend the next chapter.

I'd love to discuss how my background maps to your current infrastructure challenges. Available immediately.

Sincerely,
Alex Chen

payload.title: Interview Prep
payload.content_markdown:
## Interview Prep: Senior Backend Engineer at Anthropic

### Question 1: Tell me about a time you designed a system to handle high traffic.
**Likely theme:** System design at scale
**STAR Answer:**
- **Situation:** At Acme Corp, our primary API was struggling with 2M daily requests on a monolithic Django service.
- **Task:** I was tasked with redesigning the architecture to handle 5× growth without proportional cost increases.
- **Action:** I re-platformed to FastAPI with async I/O, added a Redis caching layer for hot queries, and decomposed the monolith into three microservices deployed via Kubernetes on AWS.
- **Result:** Reduced P99 latency by 65%, cut infrastructure cost by 30%, and the system now handles 2M daily requests with headroom for 10M.

### Question 2: Describe your experience with CI/CD pipelines.
**Likely theme:** Engineering excellence
**STAR Answer:**
- **Situation:** Our team was spending 40 minutes per deploy on manual steps prone to human error.
- **Task:** Automate the full deploy cycle for our FastAPI microservices.
- **Action:** Implemented GitHub Actions pipelines with automated testing, Docker image builds, and Kubernetes rollouts with health checks and automatic rollback.
- **Result:** Deploy time dropped from 40 minutes to under 8 — a 60% reduction — and we eliminated a class of human-error incidents entirely.

### Question 3: Tell me about a time you worked closely with a research or ML team.
**Likely theme:** Cross-functional collaboration
**STAR Answer:**
- **Situation:** At StartupXYZ, the ML team had trained a PyTorch recommendation model but had no path to production.
- **Task:** Build the feature store and serving infrastructure to productionize it.
- **Action:** Built a feature engineering platform in Python with Spark for batch processing and FastAPI for real-time serving; worked weekly with the research team to align on feature contracts and latency budgets.
- **Result:** Model went from notebook to production serving 50k users in 6 weeks; feature coverage improved model accuracy by 12%.

---

## Questions to Ask Them
1. How does the infrastructure team collaborate with the safety research team — do engineers have direct input into how safety constraints affect system design?
2. What does the on-call rotation look like for the AI infrastructure team, and how are SLOs defined for Claude's API services?
